comments.body:
## Retracted — I filed this against a stale working tree

This ticket is wrong and should not be worked. The defect it describes is already fixed on `origin/main`.

**The fix that landed:** commit `8c5687af9462dc06ec67b40185bffd2c5989a647` (Gerrit change 2990, "Reconcile a push-pending marker git disproves"), carrying trailer `rebar-ticket: 16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9`. On current `origin/main`, `src/rebar/_store/freshness.py` defines `_pending_reconciled(tracker, remote_ref)` at line 129 and calls it at line 223:

```
222:    elif pending:
223:        if _pending_reconciled(tracker, remote_ref):
```

That is precisely the cross-check this ticket claims is missing.

**How I got it wrong — two compounding errors, both mine:**

1. I read `freshness.py` from the shared main checkout at `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar`, whose HEAD is `e900fa14ad52` — **28 commits behind `origin/main`**. The line I quoted as `freshness.py:155` is genuine, but it is the pre-fix revision.
2. My corroborating search, `git log --grep='16c9-a42d' --all`, ran **before** `git fetch origin`. The commit was not yet in the local object store, so an empty result looked like confirmation. It was absence of data, not evidence of absence.

The two errors agreed with each other, which is what made the false conclusion feel solid.

**The symptom I actually experienced was real**, and is now explained without a new defect: every gated write in this session ran the stale build, so it ran the pre-fix code path. rebar told me so directly and I did not act on it — each gate emitted:

```
WARNING rebar.llm.build_drift: this rebar build (e900fa14a, 2026-09-19, dirty) is
25 commit(s) BEHIND the ref this gate pinned (6a873c9a9)
```

**Closing as a duplicate of `16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9`**, linked `duplicates`.

**One genuine finding survives**, recorded here rather than as a new ticket since it is an observation about operating practice, not a code defect: a long-lived agent session working from a checkout that never advances will keep running a build that drifts further from `main` every time it lands a change, and will then read its own stale tree as evidence about current behaviour. The `build_drift` warning already detects this and is labelled advisory. It correctly predicted a wrong conclusion here.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

Every completion-gated close in this clone refused with a `stale-store: push-pending` verdict while the store was provably level with the shared store:

```
Error: the completion close gate refused to certify f46c-8a93-2eb9-4913: the local
ticket store holds 1 committed ticket event(s) the shared store has never received
(last delivery failure: push-transport-failed) (stale-store: push-pending).
```

Measured immediately after, in `.tickets-tracker`:

```
HEAD      8722fe13417826b2ddc36d6fd924339e4aa418c8
remote-tr 8722fe13417826b2ddc36d6fd924339e4aa418c8
ls-remote 8722fe13417826b2ddc36d6fd924339e4aa418c8
git log --oneline refs/remotes/origin/tickets..HEAD   ->   (empty)
```

Zero unpushed commits, by three independent readings. The gate asserted a backlog of 1 that did not exist.

## Root cause — the sentinel is asserted, never reconciled

`store_freshness` decides `push-pending` from a persisted marker file and nothing else.

`src/rebar/_store/freshness.py:155`:

```python
status = push_state.read_status(tracker)
pending = status.get("state") == "pending"
```

`push_state.read_status` (`src/rebar/_store/push_state.py:201-226`) opens `<git_dir>/rebar-push-pending`, and returns the recorded payload verbatim if `state == "pending"`. It performs no git query.

Then `freshness.py:158-165` converts that marker straight into the refusal, reporting `status["unpushed"]` — the count recorded *at the time of the failure* — as though it were current.

The reconciling data is already in hand three lines earlier. `_ref_divergence(tracker, remote_ref)` is computed at `:137` and `unpushed_count(base, remote_ref)` exists at `push_state.py:95`. Neither is consulted on the `pending` branch. So a marker written by one failed push outlives the condition it describes, for as long as it takes a rebar-driven push to clear it.

## Why it cannot self-heal — the deadlock

The only writer that clears the marker is a *successful push*, and the marker blocks the writes that would push:

1. A push fails once (here: bug `48bd-1c15-c3b0-4a99`, `fatal: unable to get password from user`). The marker is recorded.
2. The backlog is published by any path that is not rebar's own clearing seam — a later successful push from another surface, an operator republish, a re-clone. Git is now level; the marker still says pending.
3. Every completion-gated close and plan-review now refuses, because the gate reads the marker.
4. A refused gate performs no write, so it performs no push, so it never reaches the code that clears the marker.

The store is wedged for exactly the operations that matter, and the wedge is self-sustaining. It clears only if an *ungated* write (a comment, an edit) happens to occur and happens to push successfully. That is what unwedged this session — `rebar comment` with working credentials cleared the marker, after which the identical close proceeded.

The documented recovery in the refusal text (`rebar fsck`, `rebar tracker-maintenance`) does not name this case. `fsck` classifies PUSH_PENDING as informational and never counted (`_commands/fsck.py:76`), so it reports the store healthy while the gates stay wedged — the operator is told to run a command that agrees with them and changes nothing.

## Relationship to `16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9`

This is the same defect as `16c9` (`abnormal-dear-shoveler`), whose title states it exactly: *"push-pending sentinel never reconciles against ref reality, wedging every gate in a clone after one failed push."* That ticket is **closed**, with a COMPLETION_VERDICT and a SIGNATURE.

No code fix for it reached `main`:

- `git log origin/main --all --grep='16c9-a42d'` returns only tickets-branch events (`COMPACT`, `SIGNATURE`, `STATUS`, `COMPLETION_VERDICT`). No commit on `main` carries the trailer.
- `freshness.py` and `push_state.py` contain no reconciliation on the `pending` branch, as quoted above.
- `tests/unit/test_push_pending_marker.py` has 11 tests; the closest, `test_the_marker_clears_once_a_push_lands` (`:122`), pins only the rebar-driven success path. Nothing pins "a marker whose backlog no longer exists reads as ok", which is the claim `16c9`'s title makes.

So this ticket is not a regression of `16c9` — it is `16c9` still open, closed without the change landing. Worth understanding how the completion verifier certified it, since that is a gate-integrity question separate from the freshness bug itself.

## Approach

Reconcile the sentinel against observable git state before believing it. On the `pending` branch of `store_freshness`, confirm the claimed backlog still exists — the remote-tracking ref is behind HEAD — before returning a stale verdict. When the backlog is empty, the delivery already happened by some path, so the marker is stale evidence and the store is fresh; clear it and report fresh.

Keep the marker durable for the case it was built for: a backlog that genuinely has not shipped. The change is to stop treating "a push failed once" as a standing fact about the present.

Prefer reusing `unpushed_count` and the already-computed `_ref_divergence` over adding a new git call, and keep the probe's existing contract that a broken diagnostic reports a HEALTHY store, never a stale one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A marker recording `state=pending` whose claimed backlog has since been delivered reports `fresh`, not `push-pending`. Verified by a test that writes the marker, brings the remote level with HEAD, and asserts the verdict.
- [ ] A marker recording `state=pending` whose backlog genuinely has not shipped still reports `push-pending`. Verified by a test that leaves the remote behind HEAD.
- [ ] A completion-gated close proceeds on a store whose marker is stale but whose refs are level. Verified end-to-end rather than at the probe alone.
- [ ] The stale marker is cleared rather than re-evaluated on every read, so the cost is paid once. Verified by asserting the marker file is gone after the reconciling read.
- [ ] A git failure during reconciliation reports the store FRESH, preserving the existing "a broken diagnostic must not convince a caller that a healthy store is broken" contract. Verified by a test that makes the git probe raise.
- [ ] The fix requires no single CI provider. Verified by reading the changed code for any GitHub Actions or Gerrit dependency.

## Reproduction

1. Make a tickets-branch push fail once, so the marker is written.
2. Publish the backlog by any other path, so `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` equals HEAD.
3. Attempt a completion-gated close.

It refuses with `stale-store: push-pending` and a backlog count that `git rev-list` disproves.
compiled_state.title: push-pending sentinel is asserted from a stale marker, wedging every gated close in a clone whose refs are provably level
